content.value_statement: Product teams often lack a consistent structure for positioning, launches, and competitive decisions. This skill turns business context into practical product marketing plans and templates.
actual_capabilities: Defines ideal customer profiles using firmographic, technographic, psychographic, and behavioral criteria.
Develops positioning with competitive alternatives, unique attributes, customer value, best-fit segments, categories, and market trends.
Creates persona-specific messaging hierarchies with value propositions, benefits, features, outcomes, and proof points.
Produces competitive battlecards, interview questions, win-loss analysis structures, and monthly insight reports.
Plans tiered product launches, international market entry, sales enablement, metrics dashboards, and quarterly reviews.
Recommends practical handoffs, timelines, checklists, and measurement targets for product marketing teams.
limitations: Does not perform live market research, competitor monitoring, or CRM analysis without user-provided data.
Example budgets, benchmarks, markets, and targets require validation against the product and current business conditions.
Does not provide legal, privacy, tax, or regulatory advice for international expansion.
Referenced scripts, templates, and asset files are described in the document but are not included.

use_cases.title: Define positioning for a new product
use_cases.description: Turn customer evidence, alternatives, product strengths, and market context into differentiated positioning and messaging.

use_cases.title: Plan a coordinated product launch
use_cases.description: Create a launch tier, timeline, channel plan, enablement checklist, ownership model, and measurement dashboard.

use_cases.title: Enter a new geographic market
use_cases.description: Evaluate market priorities and build a phased localization, staffing, partnership, budget, and revenue plan.

prompt_templates.title: Draft an ideal customer profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ICP for [product]. Use our customers, deal data, market, pricing, and product strengths: [context]. Identify assumptions and missing evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when the team needs a focused target-customer definition.

prompt_templates.title: Develop product positioning
prompt_templates.prompt: Build positioning for [product] using customer alternatives, unique attributes, delivered value, best-fit buyers, market category, and relevant trends. Use only supported claims.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before revising messaging, a website, or sales materials.

prompt_templates.title: Create a competitive battlecard
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a sales battlecard for [competitor] from this evidence: [research]. Include strengths, weaknesses, our advantages, qualification guidance, objections, responses, and proof gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when sales teams frequently encounter one competitor.

prompt_templates.title: Design an international launch plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop a phased GTM plan for [market] using our ICP, product readiness, legal constraints, localization needs, budget, channels, sales capacity, and targets: [context].
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for advanced market-entry planning across functions.

output_examples.input: Position our workflow platform for mid-market software companies replacing spreadsheets.
output_examples.output: Positioning summary: The strongest alternative is manual spreadsheet coordination. Lead with faster handoffs and fewer status errors, supported by verified implementation and adoption evidence.

output_examples.input: Plan a standard launch for a new analytics integration.
output: Launch tier: Standard launch with three to four weeks of preparation.
Core assets: Product update, customer email, sales brief, demo workflow, support documentation, and tracking dashboard.
Primary measures: Adoption, qualified pipeline, demo conversion, support volume, and sales feedback.

output_examples.input: Prepare a competitor battlecard from customer interviews and review data.
output_examples.output: Battlecard: Summarize the competitor position, verified strengths, recurring weaknesses, best-fit situations, loss risks, objection responses, and missing proof requiring research.

best_practices: Provide current customer, product, pipeline, and competitive evidence before requesting strategy recommendations.
Separate verified facts from assumptions, estimates, placeholders, and suggested benchmarks.
Review positioning and launch plans with product, sales, customer success, finance, and legal stakeholders.
anti_patterns: Do not publish placeholder claims, customer names, metrics, or competitor weaknesses as verified facts.
Do not apply example budgets or benchmarks without checking company stage, margins, market conditions, and sales capacity.
Do not treat a strategic template as a substitute for customer interviews, market research, or controlled testing.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide product details, target customers, pricing, customer evidence, competitors, sales motion, business stage, markets, goals, budget, and constraints.

faq.question: Can this skill create an ideal customer profile?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure firmographics, technographics, buyer motivations, personas, qualification criteria, and validation questions from your evidence.

faq.question: Does it conduct competitor research automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can organize supplied research into analyses and battlecards, but it does not browse websites or monitor competitors by itself.

faq.question: Can it plan international expansion?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline sequencing, localization, staffing, channels, partnerships, budgets, targets, and risks. Validate legal and tax requirements separately.

faq.question: Are the included benchmarks authoritative?
faq.answer: No. They are illustrative starting points and may be outdated or unsuitable for your market, product, economics, and growth stage.

faq.question: Can it create sales enablement materials?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft battlecards, deck outlines, demo scripts, objection responses, one-pager structures, training plans, and team handoff processes.
